background_story: In ancient Greek mythology, Artemis, the goddess of the hunt, had a secret fondness for the humble Ephestia, a genus of small moths. According to legend, Artemis would often sneak away from Mount Olympus to observe the Ephestia's nocturnal flights, mesmerized by their delicate beauty. One night, while watching an Ephestia moth dance around a flame, Artemis was inspired to create a magical amulet. The amulet, imbued with the Ephestia's gentle spirit, would protect hunters from harm and grant them unparalleled accuracy. From that day on, Artemis was often depicted with an Ephestia moth perched on her shoulder, symbolizing her connection to the natural world and her role as a guardian of the wilderness.
